sources.entry: Amgix - Hybrid search engine built for flexible deployment and real-world messy data. (Demo, Source Code, Clients) AGPL-3.0 Docker/K8S

summary.one_liner: Amgix is an open-source hybrid search system that handles ingestion, embedding, keyword and semantic retrieval, and ranking behind a single REST API.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a REST API for defining collections, bulk-uploading documents, and searching them. Collections can mix keyword vectors (with a built-in tokenizer aimed at identifier-heavy data) and dense embedding model vectors (the example uses sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2). Ingestion is handled through built-in async queues with retries and deduplication. Search performs query vectorization, semantic and keyword retrieval, and fusion/ranking on the server in one call. The README says it can run on Postgres, MariaDB, or Qdrant without changing application code. Amgix One is a single-container image that bundles the API, encoders, RabbitMQ, and Qdrant. Client libraries are listed for Python, TypeScript, Rust, and C#.
use_cases: hybrid keyword and semantic search over documents
searching product or part catalogs with identifiers and messy codes
adding semantic search to an existing application without building embedding pipelines
fusing keyword and vector search results into one ranking
how_to_run: For GPU support: docker run with the image tag amgixio/amgix-one:1-gpu (requires NVIDIA Container Toolkit)
POST /v1/collections/{name} to define a collection with keyword and dense_model vectors
notable: Single container (Amgix One) bundles API, encoders, RabbitMQ, and Qdrant
Custom keyword tokenizer that handles missing punctuation in identifiers
Server-side hybrid fusion so the application does not combine result sets itself
Models load and rebalance across nodes based on demand
caveats: GPU image requires NVIDIA Container Toolkit
README points to external documentation for the full feature list; details of the full feature set are not in the README itself
Kubernetes support is listed in the awesome-selfhosted entry but no K8S setup steps appear in the README
